title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed
trick: Build episodes where a fact needed late either can or cannot be looked up again; truncating the context window costs nothing in the first case and drops success to chance in the second.
framing_stripped: Called 'when the harness decides success' and 'state that cannot be re-observed'; it is a 2x2 ablation (full history vs truncated window, times lookup available or not) on a synthetic 10-option recall task with 200 templates and two low-cost models, plus a one-run-per-cell path ablation of ARC-AGI-3's own harness (drop -> summarize -> remove notes instruction -> add native reasoning replay) for one model on four games, plus a descriptive per-level clear-rate table; the probe measures a context-loss cost, the ARC half attributes a published benchmark gap to harness components rather than to the model.
method_equations: Probe (sec. 3-4). Task cell $c \in \{\text{obs},\text{der}\} \times \{\text{rec},\text{nrec}\} \times \{\text{near},\text{far}\}$ (fact shown directly or derived from clues; a lookup action re-shows it or not; evidence inside or outside the truncated window), template $i = 1, \dots, T$ with $T = 200$, harness $h \in \{\text{F-0}, \text{W-0}, \text{W-n-0}, \Sigma\text{-n-0}\}$ (full history; window of $W = 24{,}000$ tokens dropping oldest turns; window plus the note-taking sentence; summary of dropped turns plus notes), outcome $y_{i,c,h} \in \{0,1\}$ = correct option at the need step among $K = 10$ options, chance $1/K = 0.10$. Cell success $S_{c,h} = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=1}^{T} y_{i,c,h}$. Window penalty $P_c = S_{c,\text{F-0}} - S_{c,\text{W-0}}$. Primary quantity $\Delta_{H1} = P_{\text{obs,nrec,far}} - P_{\text{obs,rec,far}}$; measured $\Delta_{H1} = 0.925$ (gpt-6-luna; $P_{\text{nrec}} = 1.000 - 0.075$, $P_{\text{rec}} = 1.000 - 1.000$) and $1.010$ (claude-haiku-5-5; $P_{\text{nrec}} = 1.000 - 0.000$, $P_{\text{rec}} = 0.990 - 1.000$). Test: one-sided $H_0: \Delta_{H1} \le 0$ by a template-cluster bootstrap with $B = 10{,}000$ resamples, Holm-corrected over $\{H1, H3\}$, plus a model check $\operatorname{logit} \Pr(y_{i} = 1) = \alpha_i + \beta_W \mathbb{1}[h = \text{W-0}] + \beta_R \mathbb{1}[c \in \text{rec}] + \beta_{WR} \mathbb{1}[h = \text{W-0}]\,\mathbb{1}[c \in \text{rec}]$ with template fixed effects $\alpha_i$ and Firth's penalized fit where a cell has no variation; $\beta_{WR} = +7.09$ (luna), $+8.55$ (haiku). Control $\Delta_{H3} = S_{\text{single-prompt}} - S_{\text{conversation}}$ over 400 episodes, registered bound $|\Delta_{H3}| \le 0.05$; measured $+0.0025$ and $-0.0025$. Effort ratio at the need step $\rho = \frac{\text{tokens}_{\text{W-0}}}{\text{tokens}_{\text{F-0}}}$, measured $1.31$ ($45{,}875 / 35{,}088$ per episode) against far episodes and $1.99$ against near ones (registered bar $1.30$). ARC decomposition (sec. 5). $R_{g,k} \in [0, 100]$ = RHAE (Relative Human Action Efficiency: credit per cleared level by action count against a human baseline, later levels weighted more) of game $g$ under configuration $k \in \{S0, S1, S2, S4\}$; $\bar R_k = \frac{1}{4}\sum_g R_{g,k}$; gap $G = \bar R_{S4} - \bar R_{S0} = 71.83 - 9.24 = 62.59$; shares $\sigma_{\text{loss}} = \frac{\bar R_{S1} - \bar R_{S0}}{G} = 0.860$, $\sigma_{\text{notes}} = \frac{\bar R_{S2} - \bar R_{S1}}{G} = -0.427$, $\sigma_{\text{replay}} = \frac{\bar R_{S4} - \bar R_{S2}}{G} = 0.567$, with $\sigma_{\text{loss}} + \sigma_{\text{notes}} + \sigma_{\text{replay}} = 1$ by construction; registered predictions A: $\sigma_{\text{loss}} \ge 1/3,\ \sigma_{\text{replay}} \le 1/2,\ |\sigma_{\text{notes}}| \le 0.10$; B: $\sigma_{\text{replay}} \ge 1/2$. Level depth (sec. 6). $\operatorname{logit} \Pr(\text{clear} \mid \text{reached}) = \gamma_g + \delta_A \mathbb{1}[\text{Adapter}] + \delta_D \mathbb{1}[\text{deep}] + \delta_{AD} \mathbb{1}[\text{Adapter}]\,\mathbb{1}[\text{deep}]$ with game fixed effects $\gamma_g$, deep = level $\ge 4$, early = levels 1-2; reported on the probability scale as $C = (\Pr_A - \Pr_S)_{\text{deep}} - (\Pr_A - \Pr_S)_{\text{early}} = 0.44 - 0.14 = +0.30$ on the 25 published games (90% interval $[0.16, 0.46]$), $+0.75$ on the four own games.
load_bearing_assumption: That the only thing the truncated window changes between the recoverable and not-recoverable arms is whether the one needed fact can be fetched back, so the 92.5-point contrast is attributable to lost-and-unrecoverable state and not to anything else about the window (the paper's supports: the restated-at-need ceiling scored 200/200 per cell, the recoverable arm scored 200/200 with 201 lookups in 200 episodes, and the near cells showed no penalty; sec. 3-4). For the ARC half: that each step of the path S0 -> S1 -> S2 -> S4 changes one component, which the paper itself says fails in part (the replay step bundles replay with the provider's item format, and in three games the S1 -> S2 step also changes the summary budget from 8,192 to 65,536 tokens under amendment R7; sec. 5, 'How firm this is').
weakest_component: The ARC decomposition at one counted run per configuration and game (16 counted runs, 21 total), where run-to-run spread is as large as the component effects: FT09 S0 scored 58.17 and 18.11 on two runs under identical settings (40 points apart), and the headline replay share rests on one replaced run, FT09 S2, which scored 71.43 under the frozen rules and 18.06 under amendment R7 adopted after its levels had been seen; counting the earlier run moves $\sigma_{\text{replay}}$ from 0.567 to 0.354 and voids both registered predictions, and so does leaving out FT09 (0.357) or CD82 (0.445). The bootstrap over four games has 35 distinct resamples and $\sigma_{\text{replay}}$'s interval $[0.000, 0.960]$ sits on both sides of the 1/2 bar. A critic attacks here first because this is the half with a transferable claim; the probe half is weaker in a different way: the not-recoverable penalty is 'expected by construction' (the paper's own words, sec. 9) and is a manipulation check, the recoverable and H3 arms are all at ceiling (400/400, 399/400), and the need step is a 10-option multiple choice on 200 templates with power 0.65 for H1 at the worst Holm step against a registered target of 0.80 (sec. 3). The W-n-0 notes cell (28.5%) ran on one model only; the second model's notes cell was dropped by a registered cost rule.
regime: Probe: gpt-6-luna (OpenAI low-cost reasoning model, medium effort, Flex tier) and claude-haiku-5-5 (Anthropic small model, medium effort, adaptive thinking); 200 templates x 8 task cells x 4 harness cells plus controls (9,680 episodes for luna), window $W = 24{,}000$ tokens, need-step tokens 35,088 (full) to 45,875 (window) per episode, success 100% at ceiling except the not-recoverable far cells (7.5% luna, 0% haiku), reasoning tokens 3.7-4.3x full history in the lost-fact cells; probe cost $73.75 plus $129.69 replication. ARC-AGI-3: Gemini 3.8 Flash at high thinking, four public games (FT09, SB26, R11L, CD82) chosen by a registered rule (published gap $\ge 20$ points, published runs $\le \$60$ each), four configurations, one counted run each, 12-hour clock and per-level action budgets, 49-365 actions per run, compaction every 5.6-6.9 steps in summary configurations, model calls 51-176 s (S0) vs 9-32 s (S4) median; ARC runs cost $507.96; whole study $750.11. Published-run analysis: 25 games, Standard cleared 39/47 early and 15/26 deep levels reached, Adapter 47/50 and 63/75.
information_asymmetry: Four asymmetries, concretely. (1) Harness vs environment at eviction time: the harness drops or summarizes turns without knowing which of their contents can be re-observed (a lookup or tool call re-issues them) and which are once-shown or derived during the episode and gone for good; the environment generator holds exactly that label per fact (recoverable or not, observed or derived), and the paper shows the label is the whole effect (penalty 0 vs 92.5 points). No harness in the paper reads it; the registered 'state component' that would have (phase 2, three held-out games) was dropped under amendment R6 for cost (sec. 8). (2) Agent at reveal time vs agent at need time: the note-taking sentence asks the model to restate 'anything it wants to carry forward' before it knows what it will need; its notes held the fact in 21.5% of lost-fact episodes (and when held, it was used every time), while the model-written summary held it in 92% of derived-fact episodes but 38.5% of observed-fact ones (sec. 4, exploratory), so what a summary carries depends on how the fact entered the context, information the summarizer is not told. (3) Forward vs hindsight on whether loss mattered: whether a dropped turn carried needed state is known only after the need step; haiku detected the loss (chose no option in all 400 lost-fact episodes) while luna guessed (387/400 chose, 7.75% right), so the two models expose different signals of 'I lost something' at inference time that the harness never reads. (4) Benchmark score vs harness configuration: ARC-AGI-3's published Standard-to-Adapter gap is reported per model as if it measured the model; the configuration log (loss policy, notes sentence, replay, summary budget, 175k-character vs 175k-token trigger) exists in the harness code and is what moves 63 of 72 points here. Side asymmetry for L3: billing vs token count, since dropping turns broke prefix caching (94% of full-history input tokens cached vs 48% for the window) so the window cost 2.9-4.0x the dollars at 0.84-0.90x the tokens; a cost model that counts tokens misses this. For L4: the paper measures what truncation, summary and notes cost in success on a toy where the lost-state label is known; the open item is the same measurement on real agent traces, where the recoverability of each piece of context has to be inferred from the tool trace (re-issuable call vs one-shot observation vs derived reasoning), and the paper's own result that frontier-harness replay 'recovers 57%' is one run away from 35%.
occupies: The recoverable-vs-not contrast under context truncation on a pre-registered synthetic probe (PersistGym-lite) for two low-cost models from two providers, the finding that the note-taking sentence and model-written summaries partly rescue lost derived facts, the one-run-per-cell component decomposition of ARC-AGI-3's Standard-to-Adapter gap for Gemini 3.8 Flash on four games (summary compaction plus notes recovers 86% without reasoning replay), the per-level clear-rate description on the published runs, and the open ledger (pre-registration, amendments, decisions log, $750 cost).

neighbors.title: LOCA-bench: Benchmarking Language Agents Under Controllable and Extreme Context Growth
neighbors.trick: Grow the environment state so the agent's context grows without changing the task, then score model-plus-scaffold combinations as the context lengthens; context management raises success but the benchmark does not separate facts the agent can re-fetch from facts it cannot.

neighbors.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
neighbors.trick: Fix a coding agent's loop and vary planning, action space and five context-management strategies across four window budgets on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (176 settings); context management mostly prevents overflow, and making elided content recoverable adds machinery the model rarely uses.

neighbors.title: Plans Fade Fast: Why Context Management Is Load-Bearing for LLM Agents
neighbors.trick: Hold the action-observation trajectory fixed and compare hidden states with and without an early plan exchange to measure how fast later steps stop depending on it; naive eviction drops ALFWorld success from 56.7% to 22.0% and keeping only the plan does not recover it.

neighbors.title: When Can Agents Forget Their Reasoning? ICLR for Long-Horizon Agent Context Compression
neighbors.trick: Rank old reasoning blocks by a frozen proxy model's entropy and drop the low-value ones while keeping actions, tool calls and observations; reasoning becomes safe to forget once the state it derived has been written into code, files or tool outputs.

neighbors.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
neighbors.trick: Give a multimodal model a lossless store of every past visual observation that it can retrieve and rearrange as it reasons; on ARC-AGI-3 this lifts Claude Opus 5.0 from 40.68 to 100.00 RHAE, so nothing the harness holds is ever unrecoverable.

theme_fit.why: measures exactly what the lane names: the success cost of compaction summaries, dropped turns, self-written notes and reasoning replay, with the recoverability of the lost state as the variable that decides the cost (0 vs 92.5 points), and a component-by-component decomposition of a real harness gap

attributes a published benchmark gap (ARC-AGI-3 Standard vs Adapter, 63 points) to harness components rather than to the model, pre-registered with a cost ledger; supplies a scaffold-sensitivity measurement and an honest one-run-per-cell noise estimate (40 points between two identical-setting runs) for the lane's validity questions

a side result on the true cost structure: dropping turns broke prefix caching (94% vs 48% of input tokens cached) so the truncated window cost 2.9-4.0x the dollars while sending 0.84-0.90x the tokens; not the paper's question but a measured number for the lane

limitations_as_complaints: I have one counted run per ARC configuration and game, and the run-to-run spread under identical settings (58.17 vs 18.11 on FT09 S0) is as large as my component effects; my headline replay share flips from 57% to 35% depending on which of FT09 S2's two runs counts, and the amendment that chose was adopted after that run's levels had been seen (sec. 5 'How firm this is'; sec. 8; sec. 9).

I never isolate reasoning replay: my probe's replay test (H2) stopped because the model produced too little reasoning at the clue steps for replay to carry anything (0 of 20 calls, then 6 of 20, against a bar of 10), and on ARC the replay step bundles replay with the provider's item format and, in three games, a summary-budget change (sec. 8; sec. 9).

My probe is synthetic and the lost-fact penalty is expected by construction, so it only shows the window removed the fact; I claim nothing about real agents or tasks, the registered state component that would have used the recoverability label on three held-out games was dropped for cost, and my notes cell ran on one model only (sec. 9; sec. 8 amendments R6 and R8).
